angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 577,431 km at 147.49 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7803 +/- 0.0112 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 147.49 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.83 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Rubenzahl et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1347 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..153R/abstract): 577,431 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.913 +/- 0.033 solar masses from Rubenzahl et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1347 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..153R/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5464 +/- 100 K from Rubenzahl et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1347 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..153R/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Rubenzahl et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1347 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..153R/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1347.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.560, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
